items.title: Controls partially obscure the fight area
items.what: In the gameplay screen (e.g., screenshot 2, 3, 9, 10, 15), the 'STANCE' and 'TECHNIQUE' control sticks occupy the bottom 25% of the screen, overlapping the lower portion of the fighters and the tatami floor. This cuts off the visual feedback of footwork and low attacks, especially when characters are crouching or performing low kicks.
items.why: This reduces player awareness of their opponent's position and their own character's stance, leading to poor spatial judgment and potentially missed blocks or attacks. It directly impacts gameplay by hiding critical visual information.
items.how: Reduce the size of the control sticks by 15% and increase the vertical padding between the bottom of the fight area and the top of the controls to ensure the full height of the characters and the floor is visible.

items.title: Score text is hard to read during gameplay
items.what: In the gameplay screen (e.g., screenshot 2, 3, 9, 10, 15), the score display at the top center uses a thin, light-colored font on a dark, slightly textured background. The numbers '30' and '0' are difficult to read at a glance, especially during fast-paced action.
items.why: The score is a critical piece of information for tracking progress and strategy. Poor legibility forces the player to strain, breaking immersion and potentially causing them to miss the score update during a match.
items.how: Increase the font size of the score numbers by 20% and use a bolder, more saturated font. Add a subtle dark outline or drop shadow to the numbers to make them pop against the background.

items.title: Move list is visually overwhelming
items.what: The 'TECHNIQUES' menu (screenshot 6) has a dense, text-heavy layout with many rows. The text is small, and the visual hierarchy is weak, making it difficult to quickly scan and find a specific move. The 'high', 'mid', 'low' labels are not clearly associated with their moves.
items.why: This creates a high cognitive load for the player, making it hard to learn and use the moves effectively. It undermines the game's accessibility and can be frustrating for new players.
items.how: Redesign the move list to use larger, more spaced-out rows. Group moves by category (e.g., 'Punches', 'Kicks') with clear headings. Use icons or color-coding for move types (e.g., red for high, yellow for mid, green for low) to improve scannability.

items.title: Excessive vignette darkens the center of the screen
items.what: The post-processing effect includes a strong vignette (darkened edges) that is so intense it creates a noticeable dark circle in the center of the screen, particularly evident in the gameplay screens (e.g., screenshot 2, 3, 9, 10, 15). This darkens the area where the fighters and controls are located.
items.why: This artificial darkening reduces the overall visibility of the game world, making it harder to see the fighters, the floor, and the controls, which is a critical flaw for a touch-based game where visual clarity is paramount.
items.how: Reduce the intensity of the vignette effect by 50% and adjust the falloff to be much more gradual, ensuring the center of the screen is fully illuminated and the fighters are clearly visible.

items.title: Settings menu lacks sufficient contrast
items.what: The 'SETTINGS' menu (screenshot 7, 16) has a dark background with light text and toggle switches. The 'High contrast' toggle is on, but the text and icons are still very low-contrast against the dark background, making them hard to read.
items.why: This makes the settings menu difficult to use, especially for players with visual impairments or in bright environments. It undermines the purpose of the 'High contrast' option.
items.how: When the 'High contrast' toggle is enabled, change the background to a dark gray and the text/icons to a bright white, ensuring a high-contrast, easily readable interface.
